reasoning_traces.think:
The divergence originates from two independent data ingestion streams—grok and main—each applying distinct layout strategies. Grok consolidates data into single files per entity type (e.g., rosters.jsonl), while main splits them per season (e.g., rosters-2025.jsonl). This creates a dual schema space where queries may return inconsistent results depending on which schema is active. The core issue lies in semantic ambiguity: the same logical data is represented differently, violating referential transparency. The conflict propagates through GSI’s probabilistic inference engine, which relies on consistent schema definitions to compute predictive intervals. In GSE, this manifests as a state transition problem where the system must choose a canonical layout before proceeding with reasoning. Resolution hinges on aligning both pipelines to a common schema, preserving content integrity while enforcing structural consistency. The recommended merge direction favors main’s per-season layout due to its compliance with work-order constraints and scalability.
